exact_missing_items: A canonical internal route payload schema must be defined in one doc (Contracts_V0.md or FinalGUISpec.md)
Minimum required fields for all route payloads: surface_id, object_kind, object_id (or object_ref), project_id?
Optional fields depending on surface: run_id, attempt_id, node_id, concern_id, attention_item_id, focus_sub_tab, lane_id, worktree_id
route payload is used by: deep links, palette actions, cmd.*.open_in_* commands, attention item primary_route_payload, and resume_url serialization
Acknowledgement model: 'acknowledged' ≠ 'resolved' ≠ 'dismissed'; acknowledgement is for advisory/non-blocking concerns only; blockers are not acknowledgeable
Activity: idle | running | paused | queued | background_active
Alert state semantics: 'resolved' means the underlying condition changed; 'dismissed' means presentation hidden only; blockers must NOT be dismissible
These three states are not synonyms and must not be conflated in any doc
Condition-aging defaults: normal resolved conditions clear in ~15 minutes; major resolved conditions persist until dismissed or up to 24 hours
Define `OpenSubject` in `Contracts_V0.md` with: `subject_id`; `open_intent`
Keep the intent vocabulary controlled and small: `open_source`; `open_preview`; `open_review`
Keep resolver-support metadata out of the contract.

State the resolution rule directly: `OpenSubject(subject_id = doc:...)` resolves to workspace-backed source opening; `OpenSubject(subject_id = artifact:...)` resolves to real document source if one exists; otherwise it resolves to transient `generated://<artifact_id>` source opening

`OpenSubject` does not carry: `project_id`, `thread_id`, `run_id`, `tab_id`, `panel_id`, `inspector_target`, `origin_surface`, `source_kind`, `backing_document_id`, `last_saved_path`, `generated://<artifact_id>`, preview persistence state, transport mode
Define `resume_url` as a serialized route-target transport in the contract layer once `route_target` exists.
Keep serialized forms intentionally narrower than the full internal object.
Let object families define only the extra anchor material truly needed for recovery or exact resume.
Decode all supported deep-link forms into the same internal routing path rather than handling URL activation as a separate system.
The existing wizard deep-link is a good precedent, but it should become one member of a normalized transport family.
Define `route_target` as the canonical navigation-and-focus contract.
Define `OpenSubject` as the canonical identity-native source-open contract.
Keep `OpenFile` as the path-based editor contract only.

State the resolution chain directly: `route_target` may land on a surface that then invokes `OpenSubject`; `OpenSubject` may resolve to `OpenFile`; `OpenSubject` may resolve to a transient `generated://<artifact_id>` source buffer
The three contracts are now distinct: `route_target` = navigation; `OpenSubject` = identity-native source open; `OpenFile` = path-based editor open
Define a three-depth help contract: inline help (short tooltip), context help (richer popover/side panel), canonical help entry (dedicated glossary/help article for durable cross-surface concepts)
Add an anti-drift rule: canonical term names do not change between Expert and ELI5; only the explanatory copy changes
Define the canonical `target_kind` enum in `Contracts_V0.md`.

The canonical vocabulary is: `primary_view` (full primary-content destinations: Dashboard, Projects, Wizard, Interview, Settings, Usage, Orchestrator); `side_panel` (activity-bar panel destinations: chat, files, source_control, github_actions, docker_manager, artifacts, run_debug); `bottom_panel` (bottom shell destinations: terminal, problems, output, ports, browser, debug); `embedded_surface` (embedded sub-surfaces: document_pane, agent_activity); `page_tab` (tab within a routed page: Orchestrator tabs)
Keep destination-local refinements outside the enum and outside the base route contract.
Use `page_tab` when the routed destination must land inside a known page and force a specific tab.
What is not `target_kind`: docked vs floating; panel width; widget slot; subview id; repo/worktree selection; browser tab id; workspace tab id
